construct: Diagnostic-test sensitivity, specificity, and likelihood ratios can vary across patient subgroups because disease severity, comorbidities, and the distribution of alternative diagnoses differ. Evaluating a test only in obvious severe cases and exceptionally healthy controls can overstate how well it performs in the clinically relevant population; this is commonly called spectrum bias, although spectrum effect is the more precise term for subgroup-dependent performance.
